**When it starts:**
- The clock starts on whichever date comes first:

**What to tell your installer or technician:**
- Ask for the ship date and the install date of the optimizers, so you can work out the start date.
- Ask for the part numbers, so you can check whether any end in "C".

**What "fixed" looks like for a warranty question:**
- You have a clear start date and end date for each optimizer.
- You know which parts are covered and which are not.
reference: 25 years, starting on the earlier of 4 months after the optimizers are shipped from SolarEdge or the date they are installed.

**Yes. Alert #72, "Module voltage mismatch," is in se-troubleshooting-alert-application-note.pdf, page 23.**

**What the alert means**
- One or more module voltages show a big difference. A bypass diode (a part that lets current go around a shaded or damaged section of a module) may have failed. (se-troubleshooting-alert-application-note.pdf, page 23)

**Checks, in order**
1. In the Monitoring Analysis tab, check whether the module voltage matches the VMPP datasheet value (the module's rated voltage at maximum power). (se-troubleshooting-alert-application-note.pdf, page 23)
2. Check that nothing is physically blocking 1/3 or 2/3 of the affected module(s). (se-troubleshooting-alert-application-note.pdf, page 23)
3. If the voltage does not match the datasheet and nothing is blocking the module, contact your panel distributor or manufacturer about how to deal with defective bypass diodes. (se-troubleshooting-alert-application-note.pdf, page 23)
4. If a SolarEdge Smart Module is used, open a SolarEdge support case and include the relevant information. (se-troubleshooting-alert-application-note.pdf, page 23)

- A bypass diode failure is the potential cause named in the excerpt. (se-troubleshooting-alert-application-note.pdf, page 23)

- SolarEdge says it is not responsible for failed bypass diodes and can't help with them, except for SolarEdge Smart Modules. (se-troubleshooting-alert-application-note.pdf, page 23)
- The excerpt cuts off at "If none of the above steps…", so I can't see what comes next.
- Any electrical work must be done by a qualified technician.

- The excerpt gives no urgency level. A reasonable reading is to schedule a visit to run these checks, but the document does not say this directly.

The isolation fault document (application_note_isolation_fault_troubleshooting.pdf) does not cover this alert.
reference: Yes. 'Module voltage mismatch' is one of the alerts in SolarEdge's Troubleshooting Alerts in the Monitoring Portal application note.
